subject: MedSys inference evaluation — clarifications, test matrix, and next steps
messages:
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>

Subject: MedSys inference evaluation — kickoff recap and attachments

Hi Bethany / Carlos —

Great to meet you both today. Quick recap from our call and the concrete next steps so we stay aligned before the test window next week. Attached are:
- inference-eval-plan-v1.pdf (end-to-end test plan, objectives, and success criteria)
- redwood-dedicated-vs-cloud-table.xlsx (feature / SLA / billing comparison we walked through)

Key points we captured: 
1) Goal: Validate predictability (p95 latency), cost per 1k tokens, and sustained throughput for your clinical summarization payload.
2) Hyperscaler baseline: you indicated existing POC on AWS/GCP with baseline 150ms p95 for short prompts and variable burst behavior under sustained load.
3) Requirements you asked us to confirm: reserved capacity guarantees, regional redundancy (us-east/us-west failover), KMS-integration for keys, and SOC2 evidence for compliance team.

Proposed next tests (high level) — we’ll finalize with you:
A. Sustained throughput — 50 concurrent users / 1k tokens each, run for 60 minutes, measure p95/p99 latency and error rate.
B. Cold-start / cache-warm behavior — 0->50 concurrent over 10 minutes to observe cold token penalty and prewarm effectiveness.
C. Failover test — route a small percentage to a fallback model variant (lower-cost quantized) and measure degradation modes.

Action items for MedSys: confirm test windows (we suggested Wed/Thu PST), provide a representative prompt set and sample payload sizes, and let us know the PO path (PO vs DocuSign MSA).

If it helps, I can also map the exact control knobs (reserved v. burst, prewarm count, KV cache TTL) into a slim matrix so your infra/security folks can review quickly — attached test-matrix-slim.csv is a starter.

Thanks — look forward to the next steps.

Best,
Vivek Kulkarni
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0182

1) Billing model for reserved capacity — you showed committed monthly GPU capacity in the sheet. How strict are the commit terms (monthly/quarterly)? Can we burst beyond the commit and how is overage billed?

Carlos / Bethany — quick answers inline, then a proposed test-run schedule.

1) Billing & commit flexibility:
- Reserved (Dedicated) is monthly committed GPU pool billing with the ability to configure burst buckets. Commit term is monthly by default; we also support quarterly/annual pricing for deeper discounts.
- Burst: you can exceed committed throughput using burst capacity; overage is billed at a defined per-token surcharge in the commitment SOW. We can include a soft cap and alerts so you don’t get surprises.

2) Regional redundancy / data residency:
- We can provision Dedicated in us-east with a warm standby in us-west. KV cache is not synchronously replicated across regions by default (due to latency), but the control plane can pre-warm the standby and seed cache keys before failover. We provide region-specific data controls and KMS integrations so keys remain in-region per your policy.

3) SOC2 and compliance artifacts:
- I’ve looped Rishi (cc) — he’ll share a secure link to the redacted SOC2 report and the evidence checklist for your security review.

Top 3 differentiators vs Bedrock / Vertex (short):
- Production-first runtime: continuous batching + KV/prefix caching that keeps tail latency predictable under sustained load (not just single-request latency).
- Deployment parity: same API & rollout controls across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private (makes switching models and failover much simpler).
- Cost-aware controls: built-in quantization profiles, autoscaler policies that optimize for $/1k tokens without sacrificing p95 targets.

Proposed test schedule (pick one window):
A) Wed 2026-09-23 10:00–14:00 PST — sustained throughput + cold-start ramp (we’ll need a 2-hour ramp + 2-hour steady)
B) Thu 2026-09-24 08:00–12:00 PST — failover and resilience run (low traffic shifting, standby warmup)

Please confirm which window works and whether we should include your infra/security folks on the kickoff. I’ll get Rishi to drop the SOC2 link and Laura to own the test orchestration.

Thanks,
Vivek

Bethany / Carlos — answers + final asks so we can lock the window.

1) Concrete failure-mode comparison (short):
- Hyperscalers (Bedrock/Vertex): can experience spot-preemption or node reclamation on burst instances, autoscaler cold-starts when scaling from 0, and higher variance in tail latency under sustained small-request workloads due to multi-tenant scheduling.
- Redwood Dedicated: predictable capacity (pinned GPU pools) with configurable prewarm counts, continuous batching and prefix/KV caching to reduce tail variance. Failover is warm-standby (controlled routing) rather than ephemeral spot replacements.

2) Quantized fallback quality:
- Typical delta is 1–3% BLEU/ROUGE-equivalent on summarization tasks for our 8-bit quantized variants vs FP16; we provide an eval harness so you can run your prompt set and get a regression report (precision/recall, token-level entropy, and a pass/fail threshold). We’ll provide the harness as a small Docker container and a scoring notebook.

3) PO for trial:
- PO is fine for the dedicated trial (we’ll attach a short SOW specifying committed capacity + burst rules). We’ll follow up with MSA for longer-term commitments.

Next asks from Redwood:
- Confirm which test window (Wed 9/23 or Thu 9/24).
- Send a representative prompt set (20–30 prompts) and a token-size distribution.
- Point person for PO signature and cost center to bill.

I’ve also included the DocuSign link for a short trial SOW if you want to sign now (DocuSign link: https://www.docusign.com/12345-MEDSYS-MSA). Rishi will drop the SOC2 link next business day. Laura will coordinate the orchestrated test run and share the load-script template.

If Wed 9/23 10:00 PST works, we’ll schedule a 30-min kickoff (invite incoming) and plan to run the sustained + cold-start tests starting 10:30.

Thanks — appreciate the quick turnaround.

Best,
